requirement:
`habeas add-input --item <file>:<line>` MUST parse the file under {cite}`requirements.references.outlines` and add or refresh one
outline input for every outline node declared on that line. A named node is
declared on the line containing its name; an anonymous node is declared on the
line where it starts. Each input MUST store the selected `file` under the path
rules in {cite}`requirements.ci.schema`, the node's selector, and its structural
hash. The command MUST report every selected node and reject a line on which no
node is declared.
rationale:
**Verdict: false.** The behavior and tests look right, but the `{impl}` marking is incomplete. One piece of the logic the requirement specifies is not marked as implementing it.

**What is implemented and tested**
- `src/main.rs` `fn[main]` (the `Command::AddInput` arm) passes `--item` through as `InputMode::ItemsAtLine`.
- `src/add_input.rs` `selectors_for_mode` splits `<file>:<line>` on the last `:` and parses the line number. It parses the file through `OutlineCache::parse`, which uses the outline profiles. It then selects every node returned by `declared_on_line`. If none is returned, it errors with `<file>:<line>: no outline node is declared on this line`.
- The stored `file` is the path relative to the project root when it is under the root, and the resolved path otherwise. `add_input_external_sources_respect_allow_and_disallow` shows an allowed external file stored as an absolute path, and a disallowed one rejected.
- `InputSelector::to_input` and `resolve` in `src/inputs.rs` store `file`, `item` and the node's structural hash, with no source text.
- `update_inputs` adds a new input, refreshes a changed one, or reports `unchanged`. It prints one line per selected node, so every selected node is reported. The "pending determination" handling it also does is specified by `requirements.cli.add_input`.
- `tests/commands.rs` `add_input_modes_capture_outline_nodes_and_refresh_idempotently` covers these cases:
  - Two nodes on one line (`fn[main]` and `fn[main]/fn[nested]`).
  - A plain-text `line@…` node, and a blank plain-text line rejected.
  - Idempotent re-adding, with the file left byte-identical.
  - A line with no declared node (`src/main.rs:3`), checked against the exact error message.
  - A non-numeric line and a missing file.
  - Comment edits leaving the hash unchanged, and doc-comment edits changing it.
- The unit test `line_queries_find_innermost_and_declared_nodes` in `src/outline/tests.rs` covers `declared_on_line` directly.

**Gap: incomplete `{impl}` marking**
- The rule that a named node is declared on the line containing its name, and an anonymous node on the line where it starts, is implemented in two places:
  - `Outline::declared_on_line` in `src/outline/mod.rs` (lines 809–816).
  - The `declaration_line` assignment in `Builder::finish` (lines 548–598), with the plain-text profile setting it in `plain_text` (lines 235–280).
- `requirements.references.outlines` does not define "declared on a line". Only `requirements.cli.add_input_item` does.
- `declared_on_line` is marked only with `{impl}` of `requirements.references.outlines`. `Builder::finish` and `plain_text` are marked only with other outline requirements (`outline_selectors`, `structural_hash`) and `outlines`.
- None of them is marked `{impl}` of `requirements.cli.add_input_item`. The references listing shows `{impl}` only on `add_input`, `selectors_for_mode`, `update_inputs`, `InputSelector::resolve` and `main`.
- This is core logic for the requirement that is not marked as implementing it.
- The code does not acknowledge the gap with a FIXME, so the verdict is `false`, not a FIXME judgment.

text: :::{req} add_input_item
`habeas add-input --item <file>:<line>` MUST parse the file under {cite}`requirements.references.outlines` and add or refresh one
outline input for every outline node declared on that line. A named node is
declared on the line containing its name; an anonymous node is declared on the
line where it starts. Each input MUST store the selected `file` under the path
rules in {cite}`requirements.ci.schema`, the node's selector, and its structural
hash. The command MUST report every selected node and reject a line on which no
node is declared.
:::{req} outlines
Habeas MUST parse Rust, Python, TypeScript, CSS, Markdown, TOML, and YAML
sources with pinned tree-sitter grammars, selected by file extension. Every
other text file MUST use a plain-text profile in which each line that is not
blank is an anonymous outline node of kind `line`. Each supported language MUST
have an outline profile that maps grammar node kinds to short outline kind names
and, for each mapped kind, states whether a node is named, and by which fields
or children, or anonymous. Only mapped kinds MUST appear in the outline; other
nodes MUST be transparent, so their outline descendants appear under the
nearest outline ancestor. A profile MAY attach grammar siblings to an outline
node, such as Rust attributes and doc comments preceding an item, so the outline
tree need not match the grammar tree exactly; attached siblings are part of that
node for its line range and hash. Every file's outline MUST have a root node
for the whole file, independent of language. Source in no other outline node,
such as top-level statements no profile maps, MUST belong to the root node;
profiles MUST NOT invent fallback kinds for it. Comments MUST NOT be outline nodes. Profiles MUST be
documented. Upgrading a grammar or profile MAY change outlines and MUST be
treated as a deliberate change.
:::{req} schema

A requirement or example evidence file at `evidence/<full-name>.json` MUST be a JSON object with exactly `requirement` or `example`, `determination`, `rationale`, and `inputs`. The definition text and rationale MUST be nonempty strings, `determination` MUST use one of the outcomes defined by {cite}`requirements.ci.outcomes`, and `inputs` MUST be an array. Every evidence input MUST have exactly one of three forms: an outline input with `file`, `item`, and `hash`; a requirements input with `requirements`, `matches`, and `text`; or a definition input with `definition` and `text`. File paths MUST resolve to permitted inputs under {cite}`requirements.ci.input_containment`. Project-local paths SHOULD be recorded relative to the project for portability; absolute and parent-relative paths MAY be used when their resolved targets are permitted. `matches` MUST be an array of distinct full definition names, `hash` MUST be a lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 digest, and `text` MUST be a nonempty array of strings. Evidence MUST NOT store source text for outline inputs.
:::{definition} definition_selection
:phrase: definition selection
A full requirement or example name, or a definition glob, identifying the
requirements and named examples it matches under
{cite}`requirements.references.definition_globs`. A name without `*` selects
exactly that definition.
